newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia sugar beet harvest revised down to 16 mln T.
newsitem.headline: Russia sugar beet harvest revised down to 16 mln T.

text.p: Russia's 1996 sugar beet harvest will be 16 million tonnes, not 17.1 million tonnes as was previously estimated, Viktor Sukhachyov, deputy head of the sugar beet producers' association, Rossakhsvyokla, said on Thursday.
"Seventeen million tonnes categorically will not happen. The harvest will be 16 million...If conditions are not favourable -- rain and frost -- then even that level may not be reached," he said.
Last year's official harvest was 19.1 million tonnes.
Sukhachyov said that as of September 30, beets had been gathered from 260,700 hectares, against 686,000 at the same time last year.
He said 260,700 ha was about 26 percent of the 1.015 million ha sown to beet.
Weather delays, complounded by a lack of machinery, had slowed the harvest, he said.
"There has been rain in many areas, but most importantly, our equipment is getting worse and worse," he said.
